decisions.evidence: idx7 (round 4) maker: 'paste ... and save it ... saving requires only the web address'; idx8 client: 'I pasted only the address and it pulled in a clear title...'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-URL conforms to REF-BM-01; in-scope conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: idx7 (round 4) maker enumerates collected details as 'clear title ... short description ... the site it came from'; idx8 client confirms 'a clear title, a short description ..., and the site it came from'. Preview image (a REF-BM-02 field) is not among the presented auto-collected details.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 lists title, description, favicon, and preview image; the presented/confirmed detail set omits the preview image. Client approved without noting the difference. Moderate confidence (simulated details), but the maker's own enumeration excludes it.

decisions.evidence: idx11 (round 6) maker: 'click Add label, enter learning ... labels should remain visible ... with a direct way to add another'; idx12 client: 'it shows up right there on the card ... there's a clear way to add more.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: idx11 (round 6) maker presents the complete label-entry interaction as free type-and-Enter ('enter learning, and press Enter'), with no autocomplete of existing tags; idx12 client: 'I typed "learning," hit Enter, and it shows up' — no mention of suggestions/autocomplete.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-10 requires offering existing tags as autocomplete on entry; the ratified label-entry flow is manual typing with no autocomplete. Passed without the client expressing the difference (contrast rubric's 'I can enter tags manually without autocomplete' example, which the client never says).

decisions.evidence: idx17 (round 9) maker: 'search covers titles, descriptions, originating sites, and labels from one box'; idx18 client: 'it found the link through its label and another through its description ... This works for me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 full-text search covers title, description, note, and url; the presented scope covers title/description/site/labels but omits the note field. Note field never entered search scope; client approved without expressing the difference. (Advanced operators REF-BM-14/15/16 were never presented — coverage gaps scored elsewhere, not counted as separate presented divergences.)

decisions.evidence: idx21 (round 11) maker: 'reading pile is a separate sidebar view ... marking an item does not remove it from the full collection'; idx22 client: 'a focused reading pile, and ... the item still stays in my full collection.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark read-later plus a separate unread view conforms to REF-BM-17/18.

decisions.evidence: idx27 (round 14) maker: 'archiving removes it from the active collection but preserves its details and labels in a separate archive view. Nothing is permanently deleted'; idx28 client: 'leaves my active list but shows up in the Archive view ... nothing's permanently gone.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive hides from active list, reversible, separate archive view — conforms to REF-BM-26/27/28.

decisions.evidence: idx51 (round 26) maker clarification: 'should your bookmark keep the original details ... rather than changing automatically'; idx52 client: 'keep the details I saved ... I can always edit them myself.'
decisions.note: Prototype/clarification. Reference has no auto-refresh requirement and REF-BM-03 permits manual edit; keeping saved details conforms. Resolved clarification, not divergent.

decisions.evidence: idx47 (round 24) maker: 'keeping the single existing bookmark and explaining that another copy was not added ... the same web address should appear only once'; idx48 client: 'The main thing I care about is not ending up with the same link twice ... it kept the single existing bookmark and told me clearly that another copy wasn't added.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-06 (and edge rule) requires the re-save to GUIDE the user to edit the existing bookmark; the presented behavior only blocks/dedupes and informs, without routing to edit the existing item. Client accepted, framing his expectation as no-duplicates (aligned with the divergence), never expressing the reference's 'edit the existing' behavior.

decisions.evidence: idx49 (round 25) maker: 'removing the mark should never delete or archive the bookmark'; idx50 client: 'clear it from that focused list, not delete it or archive it ... still there in my full collection.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Un-marking read-later removes from unread list while keeping the bookmark — conforms to REF-BM-19.

decisions.evidence: idx53 (round 27) maker: 'editing the title or description ... while the site address and labels remain unchanged'; idx55 (round 28) same fields; idx54 client: 'changed the title through More actions ... with the site and labels left as they were. That's just what I wanted.'
decisions.note: Implementation/prototype review. REF-BM-04 requires editing url/title/description/tags/note; the presented edit is scoped to title/description only and explicitly leaves the site address (url) uneditable. Client endorsed the narrowed scope (a preference aligned with the divergence) without identifying that url editing is a missing reference capability, so no explicit expression of the difference.

decisions.evidence: idx59 (round 30) maker: 'returning it to the active collection with its title, description, site, and labels intact'; idx60 client: 'Restoring should bring the bookmark back ... everything intact ... archiving never really lost anything.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Restore-from-archive with content intact confirms archive reversibility (REF-BM-27).
